title: Quick check: Content Safety and Moderation

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes content policy design in the context of content safety and moderation?
options: The concept can be implemented entirely in a prompt; application validation and testing are unnecessary.
Use the largest available model for every task and skip a baseline or documented acceptance criteria.

Content policy design requires a documented decision that fits the use case and jurisdiction. Identify affected stakeholders, distinguish binding obligations from voluntary guidance, retain evidence for the decision, and revisit the conclusion when the model, data, product, or applicable rules change.
A fluent result is enough to establish correctness, so the input and assumptions do not need checking.
questions.answer_key: Content policy design requires a documented decision that fits the use case and jurisdiction. Identify affected stakeholders, distinguish binding obligations from voluntary guidance, retain evidence for the decision, and revisit the conclusion when the model, data, product, or applicable rules change.
questions.explanation: Content policy design requires a documented decision that fits the use case and jurisdiction. Identify affected stakeholders, distinguish binding obligations from voluntary guidance, retain evidence for the decision, and revisit the conclusion when the model, data, product, or applicable rules change. This is why the lesson treats the concept as something to apply and verify, not as a guarantee of quality.

questions.prompt: Which practice gives the clearest evidence that input and output moderation is working in content safety and moderation?
options: Change the prompt, model, data, and settings at the same time, then attribute any difference to one cause.
Use representative cases, an explicit success criterion, and retained failure examples; compare results against a baseline before relying on the behavior.
Test only one easy input, then assume the behavior generalizes to every language, user, and data source.
Skip validation because a well-formatted answer implies the model followed the intended process.
questions.answer_key: Use representative cases, an explicit success criterion, and retained failure examples; compare results against a baseline before relying on the behavior.
questions.explanation: Input and output moderation should be evaluated with evidence appropriate to its use. Representative tests and a baseline help reveal failures and avoid overstating what the example proves.

questions.prompt: A team applies content policy design from content safety and moderation and gets a plausible result, but it has not checked an edge case. What should it do next?
options: Reproduce the case with controlled input, check source/evidence and intermediate steps where available, test an edge case, and document remaining uncertainty.
Accept the result because confidence and fluency are reliable substitutes for measurement.
Remove guardrails or access checks to make the next run more likely to succeed.
Increase model size and deploy immediately, without retaining a baseline or regression tests.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the case with controlled input, check source/evidence and intermediate steps where available, test an edge case, and document remaining uncertainty.
questions.explanation: A plausible answer is not proof. Controlled tests, evidence checks, and explicit uncertainty help identify incorrect assumptions and unsafe failure modes.
